decisive_items: Small red node and mild joint deformity at distal interphalangeal joint of left index finger
Hebreden node at DIP of the left index finger of the case
response.rationale: The presence of a Hebreden node and joint deformity at the distal interphalangeal joint, along with morning stiffness and multiple joint involvement, suggests Psoriatic Arthritis as the most likely diagnosis. The temporal relationship between vaccination and symptom onset also supports Post-vaccination Reactive Arthritis as a possible diagnosis, but the specific findings of the Hebreden node and joint deformity are more characteristic of Psoriatic Arthritis.

rejected.why: Negative Rheumatoid factor (RF) and normal anti-CCP antibodies contradict Rheumatoid Arthritis diagnosis
Morning stiffness is not typical of Osteoarthritis
Lack of specific findings characteristic of Reactive Arthritis
Limited evidence of Spondyloarthritis beyond back pain and paresthesia
SARS-CoV-2 related arthritis is less likely given the presence of specific findings characteristic of other diagnoses
